The experimental results collectively validate the system's capability to operate effectively under intermittent charging conditions, a key requirement for integrating with variable renewable energy sources like solar thermal. A physics-informed reduced order model that can predict the spatial and transient temperature distribution of sulfur and heat transfer fluid (HTF) was developed and validated using data collected from the pilot prototype testing. The validated sulfur TES Page 81 of 87 DE-EE0009329 Element 16 Technologies, Inc. performance characterization tool was integrated with a cost model and a concentrated solar thermal (CST) performance model to investigate the technoeconomic of the system for process heat application. The technoeconomic results showed that the integration of sulfur TES significantly improves solar utilization and technoeconomic benefits of CST for industrial process heat. The hybrid CST + sulfur TES + backup boiler configuration achieved a lower levelized cost of heat (LCOH) than a stand-alone natural gas boiler for a range of carbon emission price scenarios and multiple locations, indicating that large- scale sulfur TES integrated with CST offers a sustainable and economically viable solution for accelerating the decarbonization of industrial process heat. At an industrial facility located in Trona, California the lower LCOH of the hybrid system was 3.2 cents/kWh compared with 3.8 cents/kWh for process heat supplied solely by the natural gas boiler. This integrated modeling framework enables Element 16 to conduct location- specific annual simulations and technoeconomic analysis to identify the optimal configuration for various industrial process heat application requirements and market conditions. The project also generated the first unsubsidized, paid purchase orders for engineering design of a sulfur TES pilot integrated with solar thermal for enhanced oil recovery. In addition, Element 16 was awarded funding from the California Energy Commission to deploy a sulfur TES pilot at a large industrial facility to support transition from coal cogeneration to solar energy. Overall, the project validated material compatibility, system performance, and techno- economic feasibility of molten sulfur TES operating up to 300 oC for decarbonizing industrial process heat applications in the temperature range of 120-250 oC that accounts for roughly 60% of US IPH demand (about 6,500 TBtu annually). Path Forward: As molten sulfur TES transitions from pilot scale demonstration toward industrial deployments, it is important to address the engineering and operational challenges associated with scaling the technology. Based on discussions with fabrication partners and freight regulations, a horizontal single-tank design that can be factory-fabricated and shipped limits the practical capacity of sulfur TES operating up to 300 oC to approximately 10-15 MWh for process steam applications in the 120 – 200 oC temperature range. While multiple units can be fabricated and shipped to achieve larger capacities, a single large vessel offers greater economies of scale benefits. These benefits can potentially be realized though on-site construction. Accordingly, future work must investigate the logistics of on-site fabrication including the feasibility of designing and constructing vertical sulfur TES vessels to reduce system footprint and cost.
